Rice.temp_desc: Best growth occurs in warm, humid weather with ample sunshine.
Rice.soil_type: Clayey loam, alluvial soil with good water retention
important_conditions: Maintain 3-5 cm standing water during tillering and panicle initiation.
Warm humid climate with average temperature above 20°C is essential.
Heavy clay loam or silty clay soils hold water optimally for puddle transplanting.
farming_practices: Transplant 21-25 day old seedlings at 20x15 cm spacing.
Apply basal dose of Zinc Sulfate (25 kg/ha) with NPK mixture.
Drain excess water 10 days prior to harvesting to promote uniform grain ripening.

Wheat.temp_desc: Requires cool vegetative period and warm sunny days during grain filling.
Wheat.soil_type: Well-drained fertile loam and clay loam
important_conditions: Cool temperatures during germination and tillering maximize earhead count.
Strictly avoid waterlogging; good subsurface drainage is vital.
Require 4-6 timely irrigations at critical growth stages (CRI, tillering, flowering).
farming_practices: Sow using seed-cum-fertilizer drill at 20-22 cm row spacing.
First irrigation must be applied at Crown Root Initiation (21 days after sowing).
Apply nitrogen in split doses: 50% basal, 25% at 1st irrigation, 25% at 2nd irrigation.

Maize.temp_desc: Prefers warm sunny climate; susceptible to early frost and stagnant water.
Maize.soil_type: Deep, fertile, well-drained sandy loam or silt loam
important_conditions: High sensitivity to water stagnation; field must have drainage channels.
Ample sunlight and uniform soil moisture during tasseling and silking.
Deep friable seedbed with rich organic matter encourages strong root anchorage.
farming_practices: Plant seeds at 60 cm row spacing and 20 cm plant spacing with 4-5 cm depth.
Apply adequate potash to reinforce stalk strength against wind lodging.
Monitor closely for Fall Armyworm during the first 30 days of seedling emergence.

Sugarcane.temp_desc: Thrives in tropical warm humid weather with long sunshine hours.
Sugarcane.soil_type: Deep alluvial loam with high water holding capacity
important_conditions: Abundant moisture and high nutrient reservoir throughout vegetative phase.
Dry, sunny, and cool weather at ripening stage enhances sucrose concentration.
Requires deep plowing and heavy organic manure incorporation before planting.
farming_practices: Plant 2-3 budded setts treated with Carbendazim fungicide.
Perform earthing up in 3rd-4th month to support tall canes against wind lodging.
Adopt trash mulching between rows to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.

Cotton(lint).temp_desc: Warm growing period with abundant sunshine and frost-free days.
Cotton(lint).soil_type: Deep black clayey soils (Regur) or fertile alluvial loam
important_conditions: Warm days and cool nights promote active boll opening and lint development.
Needs 180-200 frost-free days with steady soil moisture during flowering.
Excessive rainfall or overcast sky during flowering causes heavy square drop.
farming_practices: Maintain plant spacing of 90x60 cm or 67.5x30 cm depending on hybrid variety.
Install pheromone traps (5/acre) to scout for pink bollworm infestations.
Foliar spray of 2% DAP at peak flowering to reduce square and boll shedding.

Potato.temp_desc: Cool nights (15-18°C) are critical for rapid tuber initiation and bulking.
Potato.soil_type: Loose, friable sandy loam rich in potassium and organic matter
important_conditions: Soil must be well aerated, porous, and free from hard clods or compaction.
Night temperature above 22°C significantly reduces tuber formation.
Uniform light irrigations at 7-10 day intervals prevent skin cracking.
farming_practices: Use disease-free, well-sprouted seed tubers of 35-45g weight.
Perform proper earthing up at 30 days to protect tubers from sunlight greening.
Spray Mancozeb prophylactically to guard against early and late blight.

Groundnut.temp_desc: Warm tropical weather with moderate rainfall supports vigorous pod formation.
Groundnut.soil_type: Light sandy loam, red sandy soil with friable loose texture
important_conditions: Loose sandy soil structure facilitates easy gynophore (peg) soil penetration.
Avoid heavy clay soils that harden upon drying and hinder pegging.
Adequate calcium availability in the fruiting zone is essential for pod filling.
farming_practices: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium culture and Trichoderma before planting.
Apply Gypsum @ 200 kg/acre at pegging stage (40-45 DAS) for superior pod filling.
Avoid intercultivation once peg penetration begins to avoid disturbing pods.

Rapeseed &Mustard.temp_desc: Cool crisp winter climate promotes flowering and maximum seed oil content.
Rapeseed &Mustard.soil_type: Sandy loam to clay loam with good internal drainage
important_conditions: Early sowing in October avoids aphid infestation during peak winter.
Requires sulfur-rich soil for optimal oil synthesis.
Frost-free clear weather during flowering and siliqua formation.
farming_practices: Apply elemental Sulfur or gypsum (20-30 kg/ha) during final land preparation.
Thin seedlings to 10-15 cm spacing within rows at 15-20 days after sowing.
Provide first irrigation at rosette stage (30-35 days) and second at pod formation.

Moong(Green Gram).temp_desc: Thrives in warm sunny weather; quick growing short-duration pulse.
Moong(Green Gram).soil_type: Well-drained fertile loam or sandy loam
important_conditions: Quick maturing crop; ideal for crop rotation between wheat and rice.
Highly sensitive to waterlogging and cloudy weather during flowering.
Active nodulation enriches residual soil nitrogen for subsequent crops.
farming_practices: Treat seeds with Rhizobium culture and Phosphorus Solubilizing Bacteria (PSB).
Ensure one light irrigation at flowering and another at pod development in summer.
Spray bio-pesticides or Neem formulation to check whitefly and yellow mosaic virus.

Urad.temp_desc: Prefers hot humid climate during vegetative growth and clear dry harvest.
Urad.soil_type: Deep loamy to clayey soil with good moisture holding capacity
important_conditions: Tolerates moderate drought; requires good drainage to avoid root rot.
Warm climate with temperature around 30°C promotes profuse flowering.
Avoid heavy water stagnation during peak monsoon spells.
farming_practices: Perform seed treatment with Thiram (2g) + Carbendazim (1g) per kg seed.
Apply basal dose of DAP (50 kg/ha) at time of sowing for early vigor.
Pick pods when 80% turn dark brown or black to prevent pod shattering.

Gram.temp_desc: Cool vegetative climate and warm dry weather during maturity.
Gram.soil_type: Well-drained medium to heavy loam soil
important_conditions: Thrives under rainfed conditions on residual conserved soil moisture.
Frost during flowering and pod development causes significant flower drop.
Over-irrigation leads to excessive vegetative growth at the expense of pod setting.
farming_practices: Practice deep sowing (8-10 cm) to utilize sub-soil moisture efficiently.
Nip terminal buds at 30-35 days to stimulate extensive lateral branching.
Install T-shaped bird perches (15-20/acre) for biological pod borer management.

Arhar/Tur.temp_desc: Warm tropical weather during vegetative phase, cool dry weather at maturity.
Arhar/Tur.soil_type: Deep, well-drained loam or clay loam with no hard pan
important_conditions: Deep taproot system enables survival across prolonged dry intervals.
Extremely sensitive to waterlogging; best grown on ridges or raised beds.
Long duration enables beneficial intercropping with short pulses or millets.
farming_practices: Adopt Broad Bed and Furrow (BBF) or ridge planting to protect from collar rot.
Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium and Trichoderma prior to sowing.
Spray Emamectin Benzoate or Neem oil at 50% flowering to control pod borers.

Sesamum.temp_desc: High heat tolerance; requires warm weather throughout its lifecycle.
Sesamum.soil_type: Well-drained light sandy loam or loamy soil
important_conditions: Drought resilient oilseed crop ideal for light soils and low rainfall zones.
Cannot tolerate water stagnation even for a few hours.
Requires fine, firm seedbed because seeds are small and delicate.
farming_practices: Mix tiny seeds with sand (1:4 ratio) to ensure even distribution during sowing.
Thin plants to 15 cm spacing within 20 days of germination.
Harvest when lower leaves drop and bottom capsules start turning yellowish.

Bajra.temp_desc: Highly tolerant to high temperature, heat waves, and intense sunlight.
Bajra.soil_type: Sandy loam, light red soil, and well-drained alluvial soil
important_conditions: C4 crop with exceptional water-use efficiency under arid conditions.
Requires hot dry weather during grain filling and maturity.
Very low nutrient demand compared to major cereals.
farming_practices: Sow with onset of monsoon showers at 45x15 cm spacing.
Top-dress nitrogen (30 kg/ha) at 25-30 days after intercultivation.
Harvest earheads when grain moisture drops below 15%.

Jowar.temp_desc: Drought-tolerant dual-purpose crop providing high-grade grain and fodder.
Jowar.soil_type: Medium to deep black soils, heavy loam and alluvial soils
important_conditions: Sturdy fibrous root system extracts deep moisture under drought stress.
Tolerates temporary waterlogging better than maize and pearl millet.
Dual benefit: food grain plus rich livestock green fodder.
farming_practices: Maintain plant population of ~1.5 to 1.8 lakh plants per hectare.
Treat seed with Imidacloprid to prevent shoot fly damage during early stage.
Apply balanced fertilization to enhance dual grain and biomass yield.

Onion.temp_desc: Cool vegetative stage followed by warm dry weather for bulb maturation.
Onion.soil_type: Friable sandy loam to clay loam rich in organic carbon
important_conditions: Requires loose friable soil for unhindered bulb expansion.
Sensitive to extreme water stress or sudden water stagnation.
Dry weather during maturity prevents bulb rotting and enhances shelf life.
farming_practices: Transplant 6-7 week old vigorous seedlings on raised flat beds.
Stop irrigation 10-15 days prior to harvest to allow outer scale curing.
Cure harvested bulbs in shade for 7-10 days to maximize storage duration.

Soyabean.temp_desc: Warm humid monsoon weather with good sunshine during vegetative phase.
Soyabean.soil_type: Deep, well-drained fertile black soil or alluvial loam
important_conditions: Needs consistent soil moisture during flowering and pod development.
Sensitive to water stagnation at seedling stage.
Rhizobium inoculation provides major portion of plant nitrogen.
farming_practices: Inoculate seeds with Bradyrhizobium japonicum before sowing.
Sow in lines at 45 cm row spacing and 4-5 cm seed depth.
Harvest when leaves turn yellow and drop and pods become dry brown.

Sunflower.sowing_period: June – July (Kharif) / Oct – Nov (Rabi) / Jan – Feb (Zaid)
Sunflower.harvest_period: September – October / Feb – March / April – May
Sunflower.temp_desc: Photo-insensitive crop adaptable across seasons with moderate climate.
Sunflower.soil_type: Medium deep loam, black soil and alluvial soil with good drainage
important_conditions: Deep taproot system efficiently extracts subsoil moisture.
Requires clear dry weather during flowering for high bee pollination activity.
Boron application is critical to avoid hollow or chaffy seeds.
farming_practices: Foliar spray of Borax (0.2%) at ray floret opening stage to improve seed setting.
Maintain beehives (2-3/acre) or practice hand pollination in morning hours.
Harvest when the back of head turns lemon yellow and bracts turn brown.

Banana.temp_desc: Tropical humid warm climate with high humidity and abundant sunlight.
Banana.soil_type: Deep fertile alluvial loam with high organic carbon and good drainage
important_conditions: Continuous soil moisture and high potassium supply are vital for heavy bunch yield.
Protect plants from strong winds by windbreaks or bamboo propping.
Prefers frost-free tropical climate with high relative humidity.
farming_practices: Plant healthy virus-free tissue culture plantlets at 1.8x1.8 m spacing.
Supply split fertigation with high potassium during flowering and fruit filling.
Cover developing bunches with ventilated polypropylene bags to improve skin finish.

Coconut.temp_desc: Humid coastal and tropical valleys with high humidity and sunlight.
Coconut.soil_type: Deep sandy loam, coastal alluvium, and red loamy soil
important_conditions: Abundant sunlight and warm humid conditions throughout the year.
Basin mulching around the trunk conserves critical root moisture.
Ensure adequate drainage; palms do not tolerate stagnant waterlogged conditions.
farming_practices: Apply balanced NPK fertilizer + Magnesium Sulfate twice a year (Pre & Post Monsoon).
Incorporate organic mulch or coir pith in 2m basin around the tree base.
Install pheromone traps to monitor and control Rhinoceros beetle.

Arecanut.temp_desc: Mild to warm temperature range provides ideal growth conditions for Arecanut.
Arecanut.soil_type: Well-drained loamy to sandy loam soil with good fertility
important_conditions: Soil should be well pulverized and aerated with good organic matter for Arecanut.
Ensure balanced basal fertilization and weed-free conditions during early establishment.
Maintain steady moisture levels without waterlogging during critical reproductive stages.
farming_practices: Provide proper shade for young seedlings during first 3 years.
Spray Bordeaux mixture 1% before monsoon to prevent fruit rot (Koleroga).
Adopt intercropping with black pepper or cocoa for diversified income.

important_conditions: Soil should be well pulverized and aerated with good organic matter for Barley.

Maintain recommended spacing and basal NPK application at sowing.
Scout field weekly for pest symptoms and ensure weed-free initial growth.
